A: Panel A shows bilateral palpebral erythema, a clinical manifestation of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children, directly supported by the figure caption. B: Panel B shows left cervical swelling corresponding to inflammatory cervical lymphadenopathy, a known clinical presentation of MIS-C. C: Panel C depicts a diffuse erythematous maculopapular rash on the abdomen, which is a hallmark of MIS-C. D: Panel D shows erythematous maculopapular lesions on the lower extremities, consistent with the described rash of MIS-C. E: Panel E displays round, well-demarcated erythematous plaques on the back, a feature of the skin involvement in MIS-C.

in_text_mentions: ination revealed a painful 3-cm left cervical lymphadenopathy, marked trismus limiting mouth opening, and bilateral palpebral erythema without edema. Cutaneous examination showed a diffuse erythematous rash predominantly composed of macular and maculopapular lesions. The lesions were round, well-demarcated, and ranged from 5 mm to 2 cm in diameter. They involved the abdomen, back, and lower extremities, with focal areas of confluence forming larger erythematous plaques (Figures 1A-1E). No vesicles, crusts, excoriations, or desquamation were observed. Oliguria had markedly progressed to anuria.
